page: Amazon Web Services i3en.2xlarge is an x86_64 storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance provides 64 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside an integrated 5,000 GB local NVMe SSD for high-density, low-latency storage. Network throughput is provisioned with an 8 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark results characterize the instance as having moderate aggregate throughput alongside modest per-core computational capabilities. Single-core tests show lower-tier performance, reflected in a stress-ng single-core score of 1284.28 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1053.0. Multi-threaded performance aligns with midrange benchmarks, achieving 6752.62 in stress-ng multi-core and 4039.0 in Geekbench multi-core. In memory and transaction tasks, memory bandwidth reaches 49.22 GB/sec for uncached read operations, supporting 6.48 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.35 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances cost efficiency by pairing substantial local NVMe capacity and memory density with middle-tier compute resources. Workloads requiring extreme per-core compute or GPU acceleration will face bottlenecks, but the high storage-to-compute ratio makes it well suited for distributed data stores, NoSQL databases, Elasticsearch nodes, and data replication clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services i3en.2xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor and 64 GB of DDR4 memory. Built on the AWS Nitro architecture, it includes 5,000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and provides 8 Gbps of baseline networking capacity. Benchmark testing demonstrates modest single-thread compute capabilities, while multi-threaded integer and database benchmarks sit firmly in the average tier, sustained by solid uncached memory bandwidth of 49.22 GB/sec and over 6.4 million Redis operations per second. Lacking hardware acceleration such as GPUs, this instance trades compute intensity for high local data density. It is specifically suited for I/O-heavy workloads requiring massive local fast storage and balanced memory footprints, including distributed file systems, transactional NoSQL databases, log analysis platforms, and data warehousing engines.
